iyanTools.title: Studio Iyan Tools
iyanTools.copy: `Studio Iyan Tools` is a unified Blender addon suite that bundles multiple production helpers under a single sidebar tab. The suite installs as one addon and renders under `View3D > Sidebar > Studio Iyan`, so the user gets one install target, one sidebar category, and one place for future tools.

cards.title: Unified addon suite
cards.body: The current suite contains `Mochi Bone Cleaner`, `Mesh Cleanup`, and `UV Validation`. All three are grouped under one root panel so the package behaves like one coherent Blender tool suite instead of several fragmented addons.

cards.title: Current version
cards.body: The current unified addon version is `2.0.2`. The package is now treated as a Blender 4.2+ extension-style ZIP with a manifest-driven build flow.

meta.body: The suite is organized around one sidebar category, one root panel, and child panels for each subtool. This matches Blender's grouping model more cleanly than shipping separate addon tabs and duplicate addon entries.

sections.title: Why this structure
items: One stable place to add future Studio Iyan tools

sections.title: UI architecture
items: Child panels: `Mochi Bone Cleaner`, `Mesh Cleanup`, `UV Validation`
One tab with subtools, instead of multiple independent addon tabs

entries.title: `Mochi Bone Cleaner`
entries.body: Classifies generated or retargeted leftover bones, keeps weighted or protected bones, exposes ambiguous structural bones for review, and deletes only entries classified as `SAFE_DELETE`.

entries.title: `Mesh Cleanup`
entries.body: Scans for loose geometry, degenerate faces, overlapping duplicate faces, and duplicate verts, then exposes guarded cleanup operators and quick-fix flows for common repair tasks.

entries.title: `UV Validation`
entries.body: Detects zero-area or collapsed UV faces, tiny or thin UV islands, and missing UV-map cases across targets, then reports per-run summaries and selection results.

sections.title: Installation
items: Build or download the packaged ZIP.
In Blender 4.2 or newer, open the extension preferences.

entries.title: Local build
entries.body: Build the installable ZIP locally with `python scripts/package_addon.py`.

entries.title: Expected output
entries.body: The current packaged output is expected to look like `dist/iyan_kim_tools-2.0.2.zip`, with `blender_manifest.toml` and `__init__.py` kept at the archive root so Blender can install the extension correctly.

entries.title: GitHub Actions packaging
entries.body: `.github/workflows/package-addon.yml` builds the ZIP on pushes to `main` or `master`, publishes tagged releases such as `v2.0.0`, and supports manual `workflow_dispatch` packaging.

sections.title: Suite-level data flow
items: The root addon registers the suite parent panel and each subtool panel.
All tool panels render under the shared `Studio Iyan` sidebar category.
Each tool then runs its own scan, classification, validation, or cleanup flow inside the unified suite shell.

sections.title: What changed in 2.0.0
items: Removed the old standalone addon directories from the active codebase.
Moved the UI into a single `Studio Iyan` sidebar category.
Reframed each tool as a subpanel under one parent panel.
Kept the improved Mochi Bone Cleaner analysis logic from `1.1.0`.
Switched packaging to build a manifest-based extension ZIP.
Added CI validation for the suite source files and manifest before packaging.

sections.title: Limitations
items: `Mesh Cleanup` and `UV Validation` are integrated as suite modules, but they are not yet fully split into smaller internal files.
Blender runtime verification still needs to happen inside Blender for operator behavior, overlay behavior, and panel layout.

action.title: Download packaged releases
action.body: Use the GitHub Releases page to get the packaged extension ZIP builds for `Studio Iyan Tools`.
